tagging_basis: AQA 7037 specification codes; AS units mapped to the matching A-level leaf

units.summary: Explain the concept of negative feedback within the carbon cycle.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 explanation of one systems concept with a familiar example; recall.

units.summary: Analyse changes in the terrestrial water system caused by human activity and climate change.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 analysis of a map/graph of water storage change; data manipulation, no recall.

units.summary: Using a figure on regional forest cover change and own knowledge, assess resulting challenges.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO1=2 AO2=4 short assess applying deforestation and carbon budget knowledge to data.

units.summary: Assess whether adapting to climate change should take priority over restoring pre-industrial atmospheric carbon.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark evaluative essay weighing mitigation against adaptation; synoptic climate-life links.

units.summary: Outline the sources of water in deserts.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 outline of precipitation and river sources; familiar recall.

units.summary: Analyse the extent of the relationship between Australian temperature and rainfall anomaly maps.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 analysis of two linked maps with patterns and anomalies; data manipulation.

units.summary: Using a White Desert photograph and own knowledge, assess the role of wind in the landscape.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO1=2 AO2=4 short assess applying ventifact and wind erosion knowledge to an unfamiliar image.

units.summary: Assess how far understanding of physical geography systems can help limit desert expansion into semi-arid areas.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark essay applying systems concepts to desertification with evaluative judgement.

units.summary: Outline factors leading to the formation of fjords.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 outline of a familiar landform of submergence; recall.

units.summary: Using two satellite maps only, evaluate their usefulness for demonstrating eustatic sea level change.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 evaluation of two maps with different periods and sources; data and source analysis.

units.summary: Using a Mersey Estuary photograph and own knowledge, assess whether deposition is the key factor in its development.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO1=2 AO2=4 short assess applying mudflat and saltmarsh knowledge to a novel image.

units.summary: With a non-UK coastal landscape, assess the role of human intervention in shaping the physical environment.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark case-study essay evaluating management impacts; case study beyond the UK required.

units.summary: Outline processes leading to the formation of kames.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 outline of a fluvioglacial depositional landform; recall.

units.summary: Using a Striding Edge photograph and own knowledge, assess the role of erosion in forming this feature.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO1=2 AO2=4 short assess applying arete and corrie knowledge to an unfamiliar image.

units.summary: Assess whether human activity is devastating cold environments with little sign of a sustainable future.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark essay weighing impacts against management and futures; extended evaluation with an absolute claim.

units.summary: Outline factors leading to the formation of mudflows as a volcanic hazard.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 outline of one volcanic hazard; recall.

units.summary: Assess the usefulness of prediction in managing wildfire.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark assess (AO1=4 AO2=5) weighing prediction against other management responses; evaluation.

units.summary: Assess whether seismic hazards are always harder to manage than volcanic hazards.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark comparative essay on predictability and scale; AO1=10 AO2=10 evaluation with an absolute claim.

units.summary: Outline the concept of climatic climax in vegetation succession.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark AO1 outline of a single familiar concept; recall.

units.summary: Analyse a map and data on causes of deforestation in equatorial West Africa.
units.difficulty_basis: 6-mark AO3 analysis of a map and chart pair with patterns and anomalies; data manipulation.

units.summary: Using data on Kenyan game parks and own knowledge, assess implications for savanna sustainability.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark assess (AO1=4 AO2=5) interpreting data alongside development issues knowledge.

units.summary: Analyse interconnections between climate, vegetation and soils in temperate deciduous woodland development.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark extended analysis (AO1=4 AO2=5) of linked components of a biome without data support.

units.summary: With a local ecosystem, evaluate how far management has created a viable future.
units.difficulty_basis: 20-mark case-study essay evaluating sustainable management; local case study required.
